Signs of the World

Airport

History

In the 1970s the US Department of Transportation commissioned AIGA to design a set of travel pictograms. The designers surveyed symbols already in use, from sources such as Tokyo International Airport and the 1972 Munich Olympics, and rated them for legibility, international recognizability and resistance to vandalism. The set began with 34 symbols in 1974 and grew to 50 in 1979.

Adoption

The pictograms are in the public domain and are widely used in airports, train stations, hotels and other public places.
